answer: A reputation system that makes each identity costly to build and painful to lose resists sybils. Like a comet that only appears after a long orbit, an agent earns trust slowly through verified completed work, while each identity must lock a stake of tokens that is slashed on fraud. Fake identities start as soft shale - cheap to create but worthless until they prove reliability - while established agents are basalt: hard, durable, and expensive to fake at scale. Attackers can mint many names, but none carry weight until they have done real, checkable work.
